actionability.justification: The remedy specifies a concrete procedure (identify the verification command, run it, report literal pass/fail output or exit code, explicitly flag when it can't be run or when a result is stale) rather than a vague admonition to 'be careful.'

generality_without_vagueness.justification: It generalizes across tests, lint, build, release, and repair claims (matching the cited incidents) while staying concrete via explicit anti-patterns and good/bad examples, avoiding collapse into an empty platitude like 'verify your work.'

leakage.justification: The remedy body and description contain no project-specific nouns (e.g. no mention of harbor/cinder/aurora/lantern or other incident-specific identifiers), staying fully general.

routing_fitness.justification: Given the failure recurred across six projects and squarely matches an existing skill's stated trigger, revising that skill (same remedy type) rather than spawning a sibling or downgrading to a one-off project note is the appropriate, non-redundant choice.

trigger_quality.justification: The 'Use when about to claim that a fix, test, lint, build, check, or repair passed...' trigger names the exact pre-claim moment where the rule should fire, making it a real, checkable trigger rather than a generic description.
